How does a wing actually generate lift?

Lift is generated through two complementary physical principles: Bernoulli’s Principle (pressure differentials) and Newton’s Third Law (action-reaction via air deflection). While pressure differences matter, they are a result of the wing forcing the air to curve and move downward.

Definition: Lift ✈️

In fluid dynamics, lift is the component of the total aerodynamic force perpendicular to the oncoming flow direction. It occurs because a wing (airfoil) changes the momentum of the air, deflecting it downward. According to Newton\'s Third Law, as the wing pushes the air down, the air pushes the wing up. Simultaneously, Bernoulli\'s Principle states that the faster-moving air over the curved top of the wing creates a lower pressure zone compared to the slower air underneath.

Why does 100 GSM paper fly further than printer paper?

The 100 GSM paper is preferred because it increases the inertial mass of the airplane without significantly increasing its surface area. This higher mass-to-surface-area ratio allows the plane to "punch" through the air more effectively, as it possesses more energy to counteract the negative work done by drag 🌬️.

Definition: Kinetic Energy and Momentum ⚡

  • Kinetic Energy (KE): The energy an object possesses due to its motion, defined by the formula KE=21​mv2.

  • Momentum (p): The product of an object\'s mass and its velocity (p=mv), representing the "quantity of motion."

When you throw a plane, you provide the initial velocity (v). With a higher mass (m) from the 100 GSM paper, the plane starts its flight with more joules of energy and more momentum than a lighter 80 GSM version.
